title: Qcqs rational finite-model inputs are locally generated by integral coefficient extensions
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, a finite subextension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme $V$ [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. Let $\Lambda=\underline E$, the condensed ring of all continuous functions to the normed finite extension $E$, or let $\Lambda=\Omega^{\mathrm{fin}}$ be the finite-subextension-valued condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]: on a profinite set $S$ its sections are continuous functions $S\to\Omega$ whose image is contained in one finite subextension. This second coefficient ring is not the all-norm-continuous-function ring. Put $\mathcal F=\{E\}$ in the first case and let $\mathcal F$ be the set of all finite subextensions $F/\mathbf Q_\ell$ of $\Omega$ in the second, in the universe [def-weil-size-convention]. For $F\in\mathcal F$ put $A=\mathcal O_F$ with its induced norm topology [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], pull these condensed rings back to $V_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$, and set $T_{F,V}(J)=\Lambda_V\otimes^L_{A_V}J$ in the ordinary unbounded module-object category [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Let $\mathcal G_V$ consist of these objects for all $J\in\mathrm D_{\mathrm{ctf}}(V,A)$, with the finite constant scalar-model constructibility and finite Tor amplitude of [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Every object of $\mathcal G_V$ belongs to $\mathrm D_{\mathrm{ctf}}(V,\Lambda)$, and every object of $\mathrm D_{\mathrm{ctf}}(V,\Lambda)$ belongs to $\operatorname{Loc}(\mathcal G_V)$. Here $\operatorname{Loc}$ is the smallest full replete triangulated subcategory [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory] of the ambient ordinary derived category containing $\mathcal G_V$ and closed under all small ambient coproducts; arbitrary $\Lambda_V$-linear morphisms are allowed. In the finite-extension case this agrees with [sk-def-localizing-closure]. The generation conclusion in fact uses only finitely many shifts and triangle extensions for each input. No descent of the input complex or its connecting morphisms to one finite coefficient field is asserted. No Noetherian, characteristic, dimension or invertibility-of-$\ell$ hypothesis on $V$ is imposed.

source.place: (2), coefficient devissage needed for the closed-complement generator calculation. Agent qcqs/all-continuous norm-topological generation lemma. Hemo--Richarz--Scholbach Theorem 7.7 supports the finite rational-field comparison; its Lemma 7.9 uses colimit topology and is NOT asserted to prove the norm-topological algebraic-closure clause here.

proof.text: Work with the section-ring sheaves of the pulled-back ring objects. The equivalence [lem-sfb-module-object-ringed-site-derived-comparison] leaves underlying sheaves and maps unchanged, and [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison] identifies relative tensor, flatness and K-flatness. Thus finite scalar presentations, cohomology, Tor bounds and the specified derived scalar extensions have exactly their ringed-site meanings. At the end this equivalence transports the argument back to module objects. It preserves ambient coproducts by their universal property; all categories and coproducts use [def-weil-size-convention].

source.place: Coefficient conventions, before the lattice construction

proof.text: For every scheme $T$, $A_T\to F_T$ is a flat localization by [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-invert-ell]. For the finite-subextension-valued algebraic closure, $F_T\to\Lambda_T$ is flat by [lem-sfb-qlbar-flat]. Their composite is flat: its tensor functor is the composite of the two exact scalar-extension functors, by $(b\otimes f)\otimes m\mapsto b\otimes fm$ and its inverse $b\otimes m\mapsto(b\otimes1)\otimes m$. These maps follow directly from the balancing relations. Consequently $T_{F,T}$ is exact termwise scalar extension, triangulated by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated], and its cohomology is the scalar extension of the original cohomology by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology]. Only the finite-valued algebraic-closure coefficient is used here.

Let $J\in D_{\mathrm{ctf}}(V,A)$. Each local scalar model of each $H^q(J)$ has the two-term finite-free scalar resolution of [lem-sfb-finite-constant-model-two-term-free-resolution]. After step 2 its scalar matrix is over the field $\Lambda(*)$; its cokernel is a finite-dimensional vector space, so its realized cokernel is finite free. Hence $H^q(T_{F,V}J)$ has finite constant models on the same finite constructible stratification. Boundedness follows from the cohomology identification in step 2. For a Tor interval $[a,b]$ of $J$, [lem-pe-coefficient-tor-flat-model] supplies a flat complex supported in $[a,b]$. Base change carries flat modules to flat modules: tensoring the base-changed module with an arbitrary target-module sheaf equals tensoring the original module with that sheaf after scalar restriction, by the same balancing relations. The base-changed flat complex therefore has the same support and represents $T_{F,V}J$ by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Apply the Tor/flat-model criterion again. This proves $\mathcal G_V\subset D_{\mathrm{ctf}}(V,\Lambda)$.

source.place: Generator constructibility and finite Tor bounds

proof.text: Fix a constructible $\Lambda_V$-module $M$. Apply [lem-fix-constructible-open-closed-refinement] to a finite constructible locally closed stratification witnessing its constructibility. This gives a finite binary tree with qcqs vertices, each cut by a quasi-compact open and its closed complement, and genuine scheme morphisms from leaves to original strata. Along each branch use the exact inverse-image composition of [det-pe-topos-functoriality-inverse-image] and the coefficient isomorphism [lem-sfb-alpha-iso]. Pull back the trivializing covers and scalar presentations. On a leaf the pulled scalar module is finite-dimensional over $\Lambda(*)$, hence its realization is finite free. Thus each leaf restriction of $M$ is lisse. The use of actual factoring morphisms avoids inferring factorization merely from containment of underlying sets.

source.place: Finite constructible refinement before lattice construction

proof.text: On a qcqs leaf $T$, the lisse module is already over $E_T$ when $\Lambda=E$. When $\Lambda=\Omega^{\mathrm{fin}}$, apply clause (1) of [det-lem-coefficient-finite-descent-lisse] on this qcqs $T$, obtaining a finite subextension $F$ and lisse $F_T$-module $L$ whose extension is $M|_T$. This result applies to lisse objects, not to the full complex or its arrows. Split $T$ into its finitely many clopen constant-rank pieces using [det-lem-stratified-lattice-rank] for $L$. All pieces remain qcqs, and rank zero is permitted.

source.place: Finite coefficient models on lisse pieces

proof.text: For a constant-rank lisse $F_T$-module $L$ on qcqs $T$, [det-lem-stratified-lattice-scheme] gives a separated etale surjection $q:\mathrm{Lat}(L)\to T$ and a universal lisse integral lattice in $q^*L$. Images of affine opens of $\mathrm{Lat}(L)$ are open by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map]. Quasi-compactness [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] selects finitely many whose images cover $T$. Their disjoint union $P$ is qcqs, and $p:P\to T$ is separated, etale and surjective. Restrict the universal lattice to $P$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-stratified-finite] (Stacks Tag 03S0) to $p$. It supplies a finite constructible locally closed partition of $T$ such that every $p_S:P\times_T S\to S$ is finite etale and surjective. This use of 03S0 requires only qcqs, not Noetherianity.

source.place: Sheaf of lattices and finite-etale stratification; replace the narrower blueprint trace hypotheses by Tag 03S0

proof.text: Fix one such $S$, with lattice $N\subset p_S^*L$. Split $p_S$ on an etale covering using [lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-etale-local-split]. On a splitting with sheets indexed by a finite set $I$, define $p_{S*}p_S^*L\to L$ by $(s_i)\mapsto\sum_i s_i$. Two splittings differ locally by a permutation of the sheets, which leaves this sum unchanged; hence these local maps glue by the sheaf condition. Define $L_0$ as the image of $p_{S*}N\to L$. Over a splitting it is the sum of the sheet lattices. The set $I$ is nonempty since $p_S$ is surjective. This constructs the trace and its image without dividing by the degree.

source.place: Pushing down by the trace: construct the sum map on finite splittings

proof.text: Trivialize $L$ further pro-etale locally. Clause (1) of [det-lem-stratified-lattice-scheme] identifies a lattice in this trivialization with a section of the constant sheaf on $\mathrm{GL}_r(F)/\mathrm{GL}_r(\mathcal O_F)$. Thus on a further common covering the finitely many sheet lattices are fixed scalar lattices $B_i\subset F^r$. Apply [lem-sfb-continuous-lattice-sum]: their sheaf sum is the sheaf of continuous functions into $\sum_iB_i$, is finite free over the integral coefficients, and its actual inclusion spans the rational coefficient module. The comparison [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficient-realizations] identifies this calculation with the pulled-back condensed coefficients, including the inclusion. Therefore $L_0$ is lisse over $\mathcal O_{F,S}$ and $F_S\otimes L_0\cong L|_S$. This is a direct local sum calculation, with no Noetherian hypothesis on $S$.

source.place: Pushing down by the trace: finite sums of actual continuous lattices

proof.text: Apply [lem-fix-constructible-open-closed-refinement] on each qcqs $T$ from step 5 to the finite partition just obtained. Its leaves have actual maps to the lattice-bearing strata. Pull back $L_0$ and its spanning isomorphism, using [lem-sfb-alpha-iso] and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. A locally free integral module remains locally free under this pullback, because the pulled trivializing cover and basis remain a cover and a basis. Coefficient extension also pulls back by the cited tensor comparison. Attach these finite trees to the original tree of step 4. We obtain one finite qcqs open/closed tree over $V$; on every nonempty terminal leaf $W$ there are a finite coefficient field $F$ (equal to $E$ in the finite-field case), an integral lisse module $B_W$, and an isomorphism $\Lambda_W\otimes_{\mathcal O_{F,W}} B_W\cong M|_W$.

source.place: Refine the two finite stratifications by scheme-theoretic open/closed pullbacks

proof.text: For an edge of this tree, extension from an open child means $j_!$, and extension from a closed child means $i_*$. These are exact, restrict to the identity on the child, and vanish on the other child by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed]. If a child module has finite constant models on a finite constructible partition, its extension has the same models on those strata and the zero model on the complementary child. All these subsets are constructible in the parent: a quasi-compact open is constructible, its complement is constructible, and relative constructible subsets compose in such a constructible locally closed subset [def-weil-constructible-subset]. Thus the extensions preserve the finite scalar-model constructibility used here. A locally free module has Tor amplitude $[0,0]$ by its local free tensor calculation; [lem-sfb-tor-interval-local-detection] tests this on the trivializing cover and then on complementary children. Consequently either edge extension of a flat module is flat, and iteration preserves Tor amplitude $[0,0]$.

source.place: Exact edge extensions, constructibility and flatness on a qcqs binary tree

proof.text: These edge extensions commute with the exact coefficient extension of step 2. For $j_!$ take the map $j_!(\Lambda_U\otimes B)\to\Lambda_T\otimes j_!B$ adjoint to its identity restriction on $U$. For $i_*$ take $\Lambda_T\otimes i_*B\to i_*(\Lambda_Z\otimes B)$ adjoint to its identity restriction on $Z$. The restriction comparisons are [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], with coefficient identifications [lem-sfb-alpha-iso]. Each map restricts to an isomorphism on its own child and to $0\to0$ on the other by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed]. The kernel and cokernel have both restrictions zero; [lem-exc-open-closed-detection] makes them zero. This proves both comparison isomorphisms, and iteration proves the comparison along any branch.

source.place: Coefficient/edge comparison by the two restrictions

proof.text: For a terminal leaf $W$, extend its $B_W$ to $V$ along its branch, using the edge operations of step 10, and denote the resulting integral sheaf by $J_W$. Step 10 gives bounded constructibility and Tor amplitude $[0,0]$, so $J_W[0]\in D_{\mathrm{ctf}}(V,\mathcal O_F)$. Step 11 and the leaf isomorphism of step 9 identify $T_{F,V}(J_W[0])$ with the branch extension of $(M|_W)[0]$. It therefore lies in $\mathcal G_V$. The empty leaf contributes zero, for which the zero integral module is a model.

source.place: Identify the integral branch generators from the preceding constructions

proof.text: At each internal vertex $T$, the localization sequence of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] applied to $M|_T$ is $0\to j_!(M|_U)\to M|_T\to i_*(M|_Z)\to0$. Extend it to $V$ by the exact edge functors along the branch. By [lem-sf-derived-ses-triangle] this is a distinguished triangle. Induct upward through the finite tree: its terminal branch extensions are in $\mathcal G_V$ by step 12, and its middle vertex is an extension of the two child vertices. Thus $M[0]$ is obtained from finitely many objects of $\mathcal G_V$ by finitely many triangle extensions. This is a finite-tree induction, with the terminal case already proved; it does not assume that an original stratum is open in the union of the remaining strata.

For $K\in D_{\mathrm{ctf}}(V,\Lambda)$ choose $a\le b$ containing its cohomology. Every $H^q(K)[0]$ is constructible, so step 13 gives its finite construction from $\mathcal G_V$. Apply the truncation triangles of [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle]: $\tau_{\le a-1}K=0$, and for $q=a,\ldots,b$ the triangle has vertices $\tau_{\le q-1}K$, $\tau_{\le q}K$, and $H^q(K)[-q]$. Induction gives $\tau_{\le b}K\simeq K$ in the finite shift-and-extension closure of $\mathcal G_V$, hence in its ambient localizing hull. No connecting map is descended to $F$; all triangles and their arbitrary $\Lambda_V$-linear maps stay in the ambient category. Together with step 3 this proves both clauses. The zero complex, empty $V$ and rank-zero leaves are included.

source.place: Bounded cohomological devissage after the sheaf argument

split_report.summary: STATEMENT-DISPUTED: the unrestricted norm-topological algebraic-closure generation clause is false; report gives a continuous Frobenius family and an exact coproduct-preserving polynomial-localization obstruction. Repaired to the source finite-subextension-valued algebraic-closure coefficients, retaining qcqs and all finite-extension cases. Proved by qcqs lattice-scheme, finite-etale stratification, continuous sum lattices, binary open/closed refinement and truncation triangles. No new nodes. reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NF-2cd4f2681 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: The item now uses the finite-subextension ring Ω^fin (sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed) in its Q̄_ℓ case instead of the all-continuous ring C(−,Q̄_ℓ); the E case, arbitrary qcqs V and both clauses are kept. Unlike Q21 cdc69125, this change comes with a counterexample to the base statement, and I checked it. Take X=Spec C(βN,k), ℓ=3 and Frobenius acting by a_n=1+3^n u_n, where the degrees d_n are primes tending to infinity. This gives a rank-one L in D_ctf(X,C(−,Ω)). The functor Q(M)=D⊗^L_{R[t^±]}Γ(W,M) is exact and preserves coproducts. Here W=Spec C(S',k̄) is w-contractible, R→K evaluates into the ultraproduct field ∏_UΩ, and D is K[t^±] with bounded-degree monic F-polynomials inverted. By Cayley–Hamilton Q kills every Λ⊗^L_{O_F}J, but H^0Q(L)=D/(t−α)≠0, so L is not in Loc(G). The earlier claim from the NA review that L is in Loc via j_! of a coproduct of points fails: N⊂βN is not quasi-compact, and Stacks proetale lemma-ses-associated-to-open needs j quasi-compact. So this is a legitimate E7 correction, named in the report and supported by HRS Lemma 7.9 (colimit topology, any qcqs X). I read all 14 steps against their cited statements. Steps 1–3: the ringed-site comparisons; O_F→F (det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-invert-ell) and F→Ω^fin (lem-sfb-qlbar-flat) are flat, so T is exact; the two-term resolution over a field gives constructibility, and the flat model gives Tor bounds. Step 4: the qcqs open/closed refinement with real factoring morphisms, plus alpha-iso, makes each leaf lisse. Step 5: lisse descent clause (1), qcqs and Ω^fin only, then clopen rank pieces. Step 6: the Lat(L) scheme, finitely many affines and 03S0 (qcqs only). Step 7: the sheet-sum trace, elementary. Step 8: constant lattices, continuous-lattice-sum and the realization iso for O_F and F. Step 9: the trees are grafted. Step 10: j_!/i_* with a qc open are exact; constructibility composes by a few lines from def-weil-constructible-subset; Tor [0,0] by local detection (i),(ii). Step 11: the two-restriction comparison plus lem-exc-open-closed-detection. Steps 12–14: the leaf generators, the ses triangles on the finite tree and truncation triangles. Edge cases checked: empty V, rank 0, F=Q_ℓ, torsion. Not a duplicate: det-lem-integral-models-generators is finite type over k, lem-sfb-continuous-qbar-constructible-generators and lem-sfb-bounded-finite-model-generation are Noetherian. No SGA, no new nodes, no fixes. The split_report tool_uses (generic other-unit nodes) are accepted.
